full_judgment: 2. The case of the petitioners, in short, is that the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners and opposite party Nos. 14-28 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 96 of 1956 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge) Rangpur, for declaration of title' of 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule land and for khas possession of the 'ka' schedule land against the predecessor-in-interest of the opposite party Nos. 1-13 and other defendants. The suit was decreed on contest with costs against the contesting defendants and ex parte against the rest and the title of the plaintiffs to the disputed land was declared and it was also declared that the plaintiffs would get khas possession in the 'Ka' schedule land by evicting the defendants therefrom by the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1961. Being aggrieved the contesting defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 141 of 1961 in the Court of District Judge, Rangpur and the said appeal was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 24-7-1962. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below, the appellant preferred second Appeal No. 625 of 1966 in the High Court of Judicature at Dacca in the then East Pakistan and the second Appeal No. 625 of 1966 was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 1-2-1980. During pendency of the second Appeal No. 625 of 1966 there was no order of stay of the execution proceeding and the decree holder put the decree into execution being Title Execution No. 36 of 1969 and during the proceeding of the said execution case the judgment-debtor filed.an application under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure, putting objection that one of the decree holders Abdul Aziz was an Indian National and, 'as such, the decree was not executable and the application under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1975. The Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1975 was allowed and the executing Court held that the decree cannot be executed as one of the decree holders was an Indian National and further ordered that the Title Execution Case No. 36 of 1969 be struck off by the order dated 8-7-1975. Being aggrieved the decree holder  preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 25 of 1976 in the Court of District Judge, Rangpur and the said appeal was disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Rangpur who upheld the order of the Executing Court by judgment and order dated 31-8- 1977. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order the decree holders preferred second Miscellaneous Appeal No. 22 of 1978 and the said appeal was disposed of at the Rangpur Session of the High Court Division and the High Court Division allowed the appeal holding that there was no materials on record to show that Abdul Aziz was an Indian National and sent the appeal on remand to take fresh evidence whether Abdul Aziz was an Indian National or not by the judgment and order dated 16- 3-1988. In the meantime, Lalmonirhat Judgeship started functioning and Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1975 along with Title Execution Case No. 36 of 1969 was transferred to that Judgeship and Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1975 was renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1992. The Subordinate Judge, Lalmonirhat after taking oral and documentary evidence held that one of the decree holders was an Indian National and, as such, 112 share of the suit land was not executable and, as such, 1/2 share of the suit land the other decree holder was entitled to take delivery of possession after executing the Title Execution Case No. 36 of 1969 by the judgment and order dated 30-3-1992. Being aggrieved, the heirs of decree holder Abdul Aziz preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.8 of 1992 in the Court of District Judge, Lalmonirhat. The learned District Judge, Lalmonirhat on 16-7-1992 took up the Miscellaneous Appeal No.8 of 1992 for admission hearing and after hearing the appellants held that since section 47 CPC has been omitted by the Ordinance XLVIII of 1983 the Subordinate Judge had no jurisdiction to entertain any matter under section 47 of the CPC and, as such, the Miscellaneous Appeal was not maintainable and dismissed the same overlooking the direction of the High Court Division in second Miscellaneous Appeal No. 22 of 1978.
